- Overestimate prices during sentiment spikes (positive sentiment → model tends to overshoot).
- Underestimate prices after strong negative sentiment (model fails to recognize reversal risk).
- Model consistently overreacts to recent price spikes, leading to delayed or exaggerated corrections.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model often forecasts higher than true outcome — adjust downward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- If sentiment turns negative mid-period, model fails to reduce forecast slope — apply downward bias proportional to sentiment decay rate.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to over-predict late-period prices (last 5–7 days) — cap forecast at 1.5–2% above recent 7-day average.
- If sentiment is consistently low or volatile, model underestimates upside potential — add 0.5–1.0% buffer to forecast if sentiment > 0.30.
- Model often misses mean reversion after sharp spikes — if price > 20% above 14-day moving average, reduce forecast by 10–15% for next 3–5 days.
